input.question: How is it that your veins/arteries don't simply cut off whenever you sit or compress the body in normal circumstances?
input.ground_truth: For the most part veins and arteries are not on the surface so simply sitting won't compress them enough to "cut off" flow, but it can be significant enough to reduce flow to the point your leg "goes to sleep" , also why you should not have legs crossed when taking your blood pressure, etc. Also the circulatory system is remarkably complex and closing one pathway often is compensated for by blood rerouting through alternate, less restricted, paths.

Question: How is it that your veins/arteries don't simply cut off whenever you sit or compress the body in normal circumstances?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine your blood vessels (the tubes that carry blood) are like soft, bendy hoses. When you sit or squeeze your body, the hoses might get squished a little bit, but they don’t break because they are very strong and stretchy.

Your body is also really smart! It has little valves inside the veins (like tiny doors) that help the blood keep moving the right way, even if you’re sitting or your leg is bent. And your heart is always pumping, so it keeps the blood moving all around your body.

So even if you sit or press on yourself, your blood doesn’t just stop flowing because your blood vessels are tough and your body knows how to keep the blood moving!
